newsitem.title: CHINA: China cracks down on illegal gold mining.
newsitem.headline: China cracks down on illegal gold mining.

text.p: Authorities in northwest China have cracked down on an illegal gold mining area, blasting shut illegal pits and making local leaders responsible for keeping them closed, the China Daily said on Thursday.
The campaign in the Xiaoqinling gold mining zone on the borders of Henan, Shanxi and Shaanxi provinces had already cleaned up local rivers polluted by the illegal mining trade, the newspaper said.
Authorities had organised more than 1,000 people in the campaign, filled in 14 pits by blasting, burned down 50 buildings and confiscated 210 items of mining equipment and 653 tonnes of ore, it said.
Some local officials had supported the mining, believing it was worthwhile to let people get rich even at the price of wasting mineral resources and environmental pollution, it said.

Local township leaders had now been given personal responsibility for enforcing the ban on illegal mining and surveillance equipment had been installed to monitor ore transportation at legal mines, the newspaper said.
Chinese metal analysts say thousands of inefficient, illegal gold mines are causing huge damage to the legitimate industry, prompting periodic crackdowns by Beijing.
